rule_text: The commit message should explain why the change was made, not only what was changed.

target.value:
fix(cli): handle ENAMETOOLONG in --target disambiguation (#166) (#167)

Wrap ``Path(sole).is_dir()`` and ``Path(sole).is_file()`` in the
single-target path-vs-literal disambiguation block (cli.py) in
``try/except OSError``. When the host filesystem rejects the token
(``ENAMETOOLONG`` errno 36 on Linux when any ``/``-segment exceeds
NAME_MAX = 255 bytes; ``EINVAL`` on some kernels for embedded NULs),
the token cannot possibly resolve to a real path. Treat it as literal
text and fall through to the non-path branch instead of letting the
traceback escape.

Discovered by the umbrella #164 dogfood orchestrator: 4 of 10
``validate`` runs in tick 1 crashed with an uncaught Python traceback
on PR commit-message and body text well above NAME_MAX.

Adds two regression tests under
``TestLongLiteralTargetDoesNotCrash`` that run ``validate`` against
``docs/dogfooding-rules.md`` with a long literal ``--target`` and
assert clean JSON output, no traceback on stderr, and the documented
``provider_unconfigured`` evidence (``llm_rubric._load_env_file`` is
monkeypatched to mask the developer's local provider state, matching
the pattern in ``tests/test_dogfooding_rules.py``).

notes: Regression entry for issue #168 / umbrella #164 tick 2: the rationale paragraphs (filesystem rejection -> literal token -> avoid traceback escape; orchestrator-discovered crash mode) appear past the opening line. v1 prompt anchored only on the subject and first 'what' sentence and flipped the verdict to fail; v2 must read the whole body. If the verdict remains fail, supporting_evidence_quotes must cite the rationale paragraphs (e.g. 'NAME_MAX', 'Discovered by the umbrella #164 dogfood orchestrator'), not just the subject line.
